questions: Does the score return to about 70.8, which would confirm that iteration 9's drop came from the 0.14 m track?
Are the line losses still at 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom, and at the same bend and step as in iteration 6?
If line losses are still present, is the controller's last_direction recovery or the proportional gain the limit, rather than the geometry?
Is wheel_radius 0.035 m worth testing in the final iteration, given that it raises speed and turn rate together?

intent: Restore the iteration 6 geometry as the base (70.83, the best result): mass 0.4 kg, body 0.16 m long and 0.12 m wide, 12 mm footprints, five sensors at x = +0.03, +0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03 m and y = 0.05 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m. Iteration 9 showed that a 0.14 m track does not reduce line losses and lowers the score, so the change from iteration 9 is only wheel_track back to 0.12 m. Expect a score near 70.8 with line_loss_events at 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom, since no geometry lever has beaten this design at 12 mm footprints and ±0.03 m span.
learning: Across iterations 6 to 9, the only geometry change that raised the score was mass reduction from 0.5 to 0.4 kg. Footprint, span, track width, forward offset and body length each either lowered the score or left line losses unchanged. The line-loss floor of one per run on the s-bend and slalom appears to come from the fixed controller rather than the geometry. The next iteration should confirm the base, and any further geometry test should be a single lever such as wheel_radius.
rationale: Iteration 9 (wheel_track 0.14 m) scored 69.05, below the iteration 6 best of 70.83. Line_loss_events stayed at 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom, so the wider track did not remove the drift. The oval got slightly worse (score 104.2 vs 107.4, progress 0.264 vs 0.272, line losses 1.8). Steering oscillation fell a little on the s-bend (0.1285 vs 0.1333) and the slalom (0.1419 vs 0.1481), but this did not reduce line losses or raise progress. Both branches in the Integrator's feedback point the same way: line losses unchanged and the score not improved means turn rate is not the limit, so return wheel_track to 0.12 m. Every geometry lever has now been tested at least once: mass is at its 0.4 kg floor, body_length 0.12 m lowered the score, y 0.07 m did not help, 8 mm footprints and the ±0.04 m span both lowered the score, and wheel_track 0.14 m lowered it. The best evidence-backed geometry is therefore the iteration 6 design (70.83), which I hold as the base. I am not adding untested changes this iteration, because the controller is fixed and the one remaining iteration is needed to confirm the base. The Integrator's controller is unchanged, so any difference from 70.83 would come from seed or track noise rather than geometry.
